newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-FIFA POSTPONES RULING ON RONALDO TRANSFER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA POSTPONES RULING ON RONALDO TRANSFER.

text.p: FIFA said it would not take a decision on Brazil striker Ronaldo's controversial transfer from Barcelona to Internazionale Milan as expected on Tuesday.

After talks between Barcelona, Inter Milan and the national soccer associations of Spain and Italy at FIFA's headquarters on Monday, world soccer's governing body said "FIFA is of the opinion that the two clubs could possibly reach agreement".
"The bureau will only examine the file, not take a formal decision," a FIFA spokeswoman said about Tuesday's meeting.

FIFA's Bureau for the Player's Status Committee had been expected to rule on whether Ronaldo can move to the Italian club after paying $27.5 million to free himself from his current contract with the Spanish club.
However, all the parties involved had agreed to meet with FIFA next week in an effort to "put an end to the dispute", the statement, issued late Monday, said about the Ronaldo case.

Although the decision about Ronaldo's transfer is put on ice, the players' committee will still make a decision about French international defender Bixente Lizarazu's move from Athletic Bilbao to Bayern Munich.
At the centre of the disputes about Ronaldo and Lizarazu are the "buy out" or withdrawal clauses found in Spanish league contracts.

The confusion over who owns the world footballer of the year has been further complicated by statements by the European Commission, which has warned FIFA that its transfer regulations may be in breach of European Union law.
While Ronaldo is under contract to Barcelona until 2004, a withdrawal clause in his Spanish contract has allowed him to buy out his deal for a reported $27.5 million.

But the Spanish Football Federation has refused to issue a transfer certificate for the 20-year-old Brazilian on the grounds that such buy out or withdrawal clauses are valid for domestic transfers only.
